_note: Hand-edited presentation metadata merged into catalogue.json by tools/build-catalogue.mjs. Keys are category numbers. 'icon' must match a key in js/icons.js.

1.description: Instruments that probe the Moon's interior through seismic, thermal, magnetic and gravity measurements.

2.description: Cameras, imagers and laser systems that photograph and map the lunar surface in 2D and 3D.

3.description: Spectrometers and analysers that identify the minerals, elements and isotopes in lunar rock and soil.

4.description: Radars, drills and probes that reveal and sample what lies beneath the lunar surface.

5.description: Detectors that search for water ice, hydrogen and other volatiles, especially in cold polar regions.

6.description: Sensors that measure radiation, solar wind, plasma and dust in the harsh lunar space environment.

7.description: Instruments that sample the Moon's extremely thin exosphere and the gases released from its surface.

8.description: Tools that test the mechanical, thermal and electrostatic properties of lunar regolith.

9.description: Beacons, retroreflectors and radio systems for navigation, communications and precise geodesy.

10.description: Experiments that study how plants, microbes and living tissue respond to lunar conditions.

11.description: Demonstrators that turn lunar resources into oxygen, water, power and construction materials.

12.description: Telescopes and receivers that use the Moon as a quiet platform for observing the universe.

13.description: Mechanisms that collect, seal, preserve and return lunar samples for study on Earth.

14.description: Robotic arms, rovers and deployment systems that move, place and operate payloads on the surface.

15.description: Technology experiments for power, shielding, habitats and infrastructure on the Moon.

16.description: Calibration targets, reference standards and monitors that keep other instruments accurate.
